hypothesis_text: High level of NFKB, a transcription factor mediating inflammation, before vaccination is associated with poor response to Hepatitis B vaccine.
population: human subjects receiving Hepatitis B vaccination

intervention.name: Hepatitis B vaccine
search_terms: recombinant hepatitis B surface antigen vaccine

possible_measurements: baseline whole-blood or PBMC expression of NFKB1, NFKB2, RELA, RELB, REL, NFKBIA
NF-kB pathway / hallmark TNFA-signaling-via-NFKB gene set enrichment score at baseline
NF-kB target gene inflammatory module score from microarray or RNA-seq
phospho-p65 (RelA) by flow cytometry or CyTOF
baseline inflammatory cytokine levels (TNF, IL-6, IL-1B) as NF-kB activity proxy

outcome.name: Hepatitis B vaccine response (anti-HBs antibody response)
possible_measurements: fold change in anti-HBs titer from baseline
HBsAg-specific T cell or B cell response by ELISPOT or flow cytometry

required_data: pre-vaccination (baseline) transcriptomic or protein measurement capturing NF-kB pathway activity
post-vaccination hepatitis B vaccine response measure (anti-HBs titer or responder status)
subject-level linkage between baseline predictor and post-vaccination outcome
preferred_outcome_timepoint: post final dose (e.g. week 4 to month 7)

scientific_criteria.description: Participants received a hepatitis B vaccine (monovalent or combination containing HBsAg).
Biological samples were collected before the vaccine dose (day 0 or earlier).
Study includes an assay from which NF-kB pathway activity can be quantified at baseline (transcriptomics, proteomics, phospho-flow/CyTOF, or inflammatory cytokine panel).
Study reports a post-vaccination hepatitis B response measure such as anti-HBs titer, seroprotection status, or responder classification.
At least one outcome measurement occurs after vaccination at a timepoint suitable for assessing antibody response.
Baseline predictor measurements and post-vaccination outcome measurements can be linked to the same individual subject identifiers.
At least approximately 10 vaccinated subjects have both baseline predictor and post-vaccination outcome data.
scientific_criteria.exclusion: too few subjects with paired data

operational_criteria.description: Study result files (expression matrices and/or antibody titer tables) are publicly downloadable from ImmPort.
Subject identifiers, study day/timepoint, and sample type annotations are present in the released metadata.

recommended_analysis.predictor: Baseline (day 0) NF-kB pathway activity score, e.g. mean z-score of NFKB1/NFKB2/RELA/RELB/REL/NFKBIA or ssGSEA of HALLMARK_TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB in whole blood or PBMC
recommended_analysis.outcome: Post-vaccination anti-HBs titer (log2 mIU/mL) or log2 fold change over baseline; secondarily responder vs non-responder status

inclusion_criteria: Participants received a hepatitis B vaccine (monovalent or combination containing HBsAg).
Biological samples were collected before the vaccine dose (day 0 or earlier).
Study includes an assay from which NF-kB pathway activity can be quantified at baseline (transcriptomics, proteomics, phospho-flow/CyTOF, or inflammatory cytokine panel).
Study reports a post-vaccination hepatitis B response measure such as anti-HBs titer, seroprotection status, or responder classification.
At least one outcome measurement occurs after vaccination at a timepoint suitable for assessing antibody response.
Baseline predictor measurements and post-vaccination outcome measurements can be linked to the same individual subject identifiers.
At least approximately 10 vaccinated subjects have both baseline predictor and post-vaccination outcome data.
exclusion_criteria: too few subjects with paired data
